application_guidance.input_pattern: Convex saddle problem with simple exact proximal maps and known admissible fixed steps.
read_original_when: Changing proximal accuracy, extrapolation, steps, dimension, test-set interpretation or output.
Using global-gap extensions or claiming Oracle Complexity optimality.
Checking the detailed energy and cluster-point arguments beyond this source Proof map.
sensitive_conditions: Strict step-product condition; theta=1; exact proximal updates; averaging indices begin at 1.
Restricted gap depends on the chosen bounded test sets; nonnegativity requires inclusion of a saddle-point.
Raw convergence uses finite dimension and is not a quantitative raw-iterate gap statement.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic explicit D(B1,B2)/N upper bound and Theorem 1(b,c) convergence conclusions.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: D is the displayed supremum of initial squared distances divided by the corresponding steps. No dimension-free arithmetic-runtime claim, minimax optimality statement, or lower bound is extracted.
complexity_scope.oracle: Products with K and K* and exact prox_{sigma F*}, prox_{tau G}; no reduction to a gradient-only Oracle is supplied.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Updated-iterate averages 1..N for bounded-test restricted gap; entire raw sequence for asymptotic convergence only.
complexity_scope.regime: tau,sigma>0, tau sigma L^2<1, theta=1; a saddle-point exists; finite-dimensional source setting.
complexity_scope.resource: N iterations require N calls of each of the two linear products and each of the two proximal operations; their internal arithmetic cost, norm information and optional gap evaluation are additional.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Algorithm 1 Eq.(7), theta=1, exact proximal maps and fixed steps; selected Algorithm upper guarantee only.

issues.note: The source writes max/min for bounded test sets without specifying attainment. The extraction explicitly uses sup/inf; Eq.(16) is the source support for that reading.

evidence.statement_check: Visually checked Theorem 1(b,c), averages, D, strict step condition, initialization and Model against PDF pp.4–6. Added the previously omitted average cluster-point conclusion. The effective-domain test-set restriction is explicit and conservative.

content.intended_use: Use the selected proximal Algorithm as an upper witness for a restricted ergodic saddle-gap guarantee under its exact assumptions.

proofs.locator: Theorem 1 Proof, PDF pp.6–10 / printed pp.4–8, Eqs.(10)–(16) and the final unnumbered inequality.
map: PDF pp.6–7, Eqs.(10)–(12): write the proximal optimality inclusions, apply the subgradient inequalities for G and F*, and use the squared-distance identity to obtain the one-step energy inequality.

PDF pp.7–8, Eqs.(13)–(14): insert ybar=y^{n+1}, xbar=2x^n-x^{n-1}; telescope the coupling cross term and bound L||x^n-x^{n-1}||||y^{n+1}-y^n|| using Young's inequality with alpha=sqrt(sigma/tau). For n=0 use x^{-1}=x0, consistent with xbar0=x0.

PDF pp.8–9, Eq.(15): sum over n=0..N-1 and absorb the terminal cross term with ||x^N-x^{N-1}||^2/(2tau)+tau sigma L^2 ||y^N-y||^2/(2sigma). The remaining coefficients 1-sqrt(tau sigma)L and 1-tau sigma L^2 are positive. Substitution of a saddle-point gives the boundedness assertion used internally from Theorem 1(a) and summability of squared increments.

PDF p.9, Eq.(16): convexity of G,F* applied to the averages bounds S(x_N,y)-S(x,y_N) by [||y-y0||^2/(2sigma)+||x-x0||^2/(2tau)]/N. Taking the two test extrema gives Eq.(9). Boundedness and lower semicontinuity let the source pass to cluster points and obtain the saddle inequalities.

PDF pp.9–10: finite-dimensional boundedness gives a strongly converging raw-iterate subsequence; vanishing increments imply that its limit is a fixed point of Eq.(7), hence a saddle-point. Sum Eq.(14) from that subsequence index n_k to N-1 with this limiting saddle-point as comparator; the final unnumbered inequality and the vanishing subsequence error yield convergence of the entire raw sequence.
proofs.omitted_details: This is a source-linked literature Proof map, not a new local derivation or independent reconstruction. The detailed inequalities remain at the precise source locators. Theorem 1(a) is an internal part of this same read Proof, not an external unreviewed lead dependency.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read the source statement and entire Theorem 1 Proof through its ending, PDF pp.6–10; visually checked the corresponding registered original-page images. Read standing Model and proximal definitions on PDF pp.4–5. No whole-paper Proof audit is claimed.

assumptions: The saddle-point problem has at least one saddle-point.
Choose any x0 in X and y0 in Y and set xbar0=x0.
Use fixed tau,sigma>0 and theta=1 with tau sigma L^2<1.
For every n>=0 use exact equations: y^{n+1}=prox_{sigma F*}(y^n+sigma K xbar^n); x^{n+1}=prox_{tau G}(x^n-tau K* y^{n+1}); xbar^{n+1}=2x^{n+1}-x^n. Here prox_{a H}(v)=argmin_u {H(u)+||u-v||^2/(2a)}.

For the numerical restricted-gap formulation use nonempty bounded test sets in the effective domains. This explicitly restricted formulation avoids undefined extended-real differences; no arbitrary-domain extension is asserted.
statement.conclusion: Gap_{B1xB2}(x_N,y_N)<=D(B1,B2)/N. If B1xB2 contains a saddle-point, this gap is also nonnegative. Every weak cluster point of (x_N,y_N) is a saddle-point. In the stated finite-dimensional spaces there exists a saddle-point (x*,y*) with x^n->x* and y^n->y*. This extracts Theorem 1(b,c), not a last-iterate gap rate or an unrestricted global-gap rate.
statement.objects_and_definitions: X,Y are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with induced norms. K:X->Y is continuous linear, K* its adjoint, L=||K||. F* is the convex conjugate of convex lower-semicontinuous F; G and F* are proper convex lower-semicontinuous nonnegative functions as formulated in §2. S(x,y)=<Kx,y>+G(x)-F*(y). A saddle-point (xhat,yhat) satisfies S(xhat,y)<=S(xhat,yhat)<=S(x,yhat). For nonempty bounded B1 subset dom G and B2 subset dom F*, define Gap_{B1xB2}(u,v)=sup_{y in B2} S(u,y)-inf_{x in B1} S(x,v). This is the sup/inf interpretation of the source's max/min notation. D(B1,B2)=sup_{(x,y) in B1xB2} {||x-x0||^2/(2tau)+||y-y0||^2/(2sigma)}. Set x_N=N^(-1) sum_{n=1}^N x^n and y_N=N^(-1) sum_{n=1}^N y^n.
statement.parameter_domains: Finite dimensions; tau,sigma>0, L>=0, tau sigma L^2<1, theta=1; integers n>=0 and N>=1. No strong convexity or boundedness of the entire optimization domain is assumed.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every instance satisfying these assumptions, every initialization, every admissible fixed step pair, every such bounded test pair B1,B2, and every integer N>=1, the displayed gap bound holds deterministically. Every weak cluster point of the averaged sequence is a saddle-point. There exists a saddle-point (x*,y*) to which the entire raw-iterate sequence converges; its value may depend on initialization.

summary: Fixed-step exact proximal Algorithm 1 has D(B1,B2)/N restricted ergodic gap; average cluster points are saddle-points and raw iterates converge in finite dimensions.
title: Chambolle–Pock Theorem 1(b,c): restricted ergodic gap and convergence
use_when: Establish a bounded-test saddle-gap bound for this exact proximal update; do not substitute an unrestricted global gap or raw-iterate rate.
